newsitem.title: NICARAGUA: Nicaraguan government, armed band reach truce.
newsitem.headline: Nicaraguan government, armed band reach truce.

text.p: Nicaragua has made peace with the largest armed group surviving from the country's civil war, the government said on Friday.

The agreement with the group called Northern Front 380 calls for a temporary ceasefire and was signed before Catholic Church and international observers on Thursday in Matagalpa, 80 miles (130 km) north of Managua.

The armed group, which was once part of the U.S.-backed Contra rebels, agreed to move all its members -- thought to number between 300 to 400 -- into a special "peace zone" and suspend its attacks against the army.
The government agreed, in turn, to suspend military action against the group and seek an amnesty law for its members.
A government statement said both sides agreed to "a temporary ceasefire between the Northern Front 380 and the Nicaraguan army until a definitive agreement is signed."

President Arnoldo Aleman's right-wing government is negotiating with various armed bands left over from the civil war and hopes to demobilize them all this year. A total of 22,000 former Contras have laid down their arms in exchange for land and credit since 1990, when the fighting ended between the leftist Sandinistas and U.S.-backed Contras.

After each disarmament, some members re-armed and headed back to the hills complaining that the government had not kept its side of the bargain. Since the war ended, armed bands have killed 1,000 people, wounded 400 and kidnapped 600 civilians, according to army figures.
